rivers.name: Upmeads Water
rivers.label: CANON
rivers.note: the course is ours; CANON: it winds from west to east through meadows with a low ridge along its south side

rivers.name: Netherton stream
rivers.direction: north-east, from the foot of the Downs down to Upmeads Water
rivers.label: CANON-INFERRED
rivers.note: CANON: a stream beside Netherton at the Downs' foot; its course and its joining Upmeads Water are ours (GAME EXPANSION); it rises at the scarp foot, never on the Downs

rivers.name: Coldlake
rivers.direction: west to east round Higham, then south and away south-west through the meadows
rivers.label: CANON
rivers.note: CANON: a little river winding about Higham's meadows and lapping the town about; the road south is straight and crosses it thrice (a stone bridge, two fords). The course is ours

crossings.name: the Ford
crossings.label: CANON
crossings.note: the ford in the ingle of the river by the willow copse; here on the village's road south

crossings.name: the fair bridge
crossings.label: CANON
crossings.note: on the high road from Upmeads to Wulstead, late built between King Peter and a house of Canons on the north side

downs.name: the Downs
downs.label: CANON
downs.note: open, treeless, waterless chalk uplands: downs on downs, no road but the Greenway, no castle, church or homestead, only shepherds' huts; water only in the chalk hollow of the chapel pool. The extent (north foot by Netherton, south foot by Garton above Higham, about 25 miles across north to south) is CANON-INFERRED; its east and west ends are ours

landmarks.name: the chapel pool
landmarks.label: CANON
landmarks.note: where the water hath trickled into a pool: the only water on the Downs
